acceptanceCriteria: The archive fixture compiles Institution, Record, ResearchPermit, Embargo, and Provenance through the ordinary generated contract. Record has a composite text natural key and no id, the committed six-file migration reproduces byte for byte, and generated artifacts contain no collaboration name.

Context derives tenant identity from an Institution selected by archive code. Record Policy uses Embargo absence and relation-backed ResearchPermit evidence without a tenant execution fact; permit state separately controls row admission, restricted body disclosure, and deposit authority.

Record and Provenance expose create only. record.deposit creates the Record, appends provenance sequence 1, and dispatches recordDeposited atomically; the recovered Reaction rereads through Policy and appends sequence 2 through an internal Mutation. No update or delete capability is generated.

The connected PostgreSQL tracer proves Embargo expiry and reactivation, ResearchPermit insertion and revocation, guarded body disclosure, foreign Institution nondisclosure, generated-client watch delivery, application restart before durable polling, and successful recovered Reaction output through generated createApplication.

Direct SQL is limited to setup and hostile external-writer evidence. Application behavior uses generated execution, fetch, client watch, and durable poll; no archive-specific execution path, second Runtime, Search, File bytes, Studio, or new public API exists.

Two shared portability defects are closed with regressions: unbounded text Data Query parameters carry explicit null bounds and questpie.binary collation, and constant query.always Field checks carry no unused caller-input parameters. The fixture uses the natural public authoring forms rather than workarounds.

The cross-fixture report falsifies UUID-id, membership-only, tenant-equality, mutable-CRUD, and collaboration-ontology assumptions with source citations. Immutable provenance is claimed at the generated application mutation surface, not as a new PostgreSQL owner or RLS boundary.

The BETA-11 selected-PR micro scenario owns measured compile, generated-byte, and TypeScript-instantiation budgets. The prescribed changed loop, PostgreSQL 17 scenario, micro scenario, full quality lane, and diff check pass without duplicating a semantic kernel.
